sanskrit_verse:
संनिरुध्येन्द्रियग्रामं रागद्वेषौ प्रहाय च /
भयं हित्वा च भूतानाममृतीभवति द्विजः // YajñS_3.61
transliteration: saṃnirudhyendriyagrāmaṃ rāgadveṣau prahāya ca / bhayaṃ hitvā ca bhūtānām amṛtībhavati dvijaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: The twice-born who restrains the aggregate of senses, abandons attachment and aversion, and relinquishes fear toward all beings becomes immortal.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from self-mastery, not coercion.
Causation originates in consciousness control, not external compulsion.
Capacity-based responsibility arises through sensory discipline and emotional detachment.
Restoration logic operates by removing internal obstacles to dharma, not imposing external penalties.
Consciousness alignment enables right action without fear or desire.

supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that a qualified dvija's testimony or judgment carries inherent validity when rooted in sensory restraint and absence of fear or desire. Legal weight is assigned based on inner mastery rather than positional power.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through sensory withdrawal and emotional neutrality. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential liberation from reactive conditioning. Responsibility is proportional to one’s alignment with non-reactive awareness. The non-punitive reality rule confirms that true justice emerges only where fear and desire are transcended.
